name: Reverb for pads: pick type by texture, then set up 100%-wet EQ'd send returns
goal: Choose and route cinematic pad/synth reverb: decide if reverb is needed; pick type by texture not just length (hall lush 2–3s+ with mud risk, chamber thickening with less space, room/ambience intimate ~0.3–1s, plate bright attack→darker decay, spring metallic/boingy); keep 2–3 go-to returns (room ~1s, long plate ~6s, bright spring ~4s) at 100% wet on sends; high-pass returns ~200 Hz+; use pre-delay for clarity, layer short ambience under longer hall/plate, prefer shorter spaces in busy mixes, and pull send back on longer decays.

sources.title: Unlock Reverb Types-How to Use Room, Hall, Chamber, Plate, Spring

prerequisites: DAW sends/returns; reverb with hall/chamber/room/plate/spring (or IR) modes; EQ after reverb on the return

inputs.name: reverb_slots
inputs.description: room + plate + spring (or third bright flavor) saved returns

inputs.name: hp_hz
inputs.description: High-pass on reverb return (~200 Hz baseline from transcript)

outputs.name: pad_space_choice
outputs.description: Chosen reverb type + layering notes for pads/strings

outputs.name: reverb_send_template
outputs.description: Two–three EQ'd 100%-wet reverb returns ready for pad/vocal/synth sends

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there.

Original synthesis / signal-flow only — map brand UI (Ableton/Vital/Serum/VAST/etc.) to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable parameter relationships over vendor-specific preset or bank names.
Not affiliated with plugin/synth vendors named in the source videos; recreate with comparable modules.
Prefer sends over insert mix knobs so dry pad level stays independent of wet amount.
Shimmer (pitch-shifted) reverb is a separate skill: shimmer-reverb-pitchshift-plus12-feedback.

steps.action: Decide intentionally whether the source needs reverb (do not add by default). Match genre references.
steps.expect: Clear yes/no for reverb on the pad/synth

steps.action: Recall controls: pre-delay separates dry from reverb onset (clarity); early reflections cue size/material; tail/late reflections = sustain; decay = fade. Think texture/tonality more than length alone.
Hall: large auditorium character, often ~2–3s+ (longer for cinematic/atmosphere); lush/deep, thickens and pushes source back—high mud risk. Natural for piano/strings/orchestra.
steps.expect: Deep lush space or intentional depth push

steps.action: Chamber: studio reflective-room character—lush thickening with less mix real-estate than hall; very versatile (pads, strings, vocals). Room/ambience: smaller/intimate; ambiences often ~0.3–1s, ER-heavy—liveliness without takeover.
steps.expect: Thickening or intimate space without hall mud

steps.action: Plate: mechanical metal-plate density; bright quick attack then darker decay—great sustain/sheen. Spring: metallic/boingy modulation in decay—character FX more than lush pad default.
steps.expect: Plate sheen or spring character as intended

steps.action: Build 2–3 saved returns: (1) room ~1s+ decay for basic space; (2) long ambient plate (transcript example ~6.2s); (3) spring or other bright flavor (~4s). Save in template.
Use sends: set reverb mix to 100% wet on the return. Control amount only via send level so dry stays constant and wet can be EQ'd independently.
steps.expect: Dry on channel; wet-only on return

steps.action: EQ the reverb return after the algo: high-pass everything below ~200 Hz (or higher) so reverb does not invent mud. Optional cuts for metallic harshness (e.g. spring).
steps.expect: Wet space without boom below ~200 Hz

steps.action: Practice: pick type in solo for texture, set level in full mix. Layer short ambience under longer hall/plate. Busy mixes → shorter rooms/plates; sparse/ballad → longer halls/plates. Optional high-cut on reverb darkens and pushes wet further back.
steps.expect: Pad sits in space without muddying the bed

steps.action: Add too much send, then back off to a musical amount. Longer decays usually need less send; shorter rooms can take more. Share one long plate across lead vs backgrounds with different send depths.
steps.expect: Audible halo without wash; longer = quieter send

verification: Type chosen for texture (hall vs chamber vs plate etc.), not length alone
Busy mix uses shorter spaces; sparse allows longer lush halls/plates
Pre-delay and/or wet EQ used when dry clarity suffers
Returns are 100% wet; amount via sends
Each return has post-reverb HPF ~200 Hz+
Template has room + long plate + bright third option
